stem_book: [One or more than one option may be correct] Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct about the ionic product of water? (a) K_i (ionization constant of water) < K_w (ionic product of water) (b) pK_i > pK_w (c) At 25 °C, K_i = 1.8×10⁻¹⁴ (d) Ionic product of water at 10 °C is 10⁻¹⁴
key: (a), (b) K i < K w and pK i > pK w
reason: Subscripts restored (K_i, K_w) and option (c) given its 'At'.
work: K_i = Kw/[H₂O] = 10⁻¹⁴/55.5 = 1.8×10⁻¹⁶ < Kw ⇒ pK_i 15.74 > pK_w 14; (c) wrong power; Kw(10 °C) ≈ 0.29×10⁻¹⁴
